card.name: Buchimish
card.era: Traditional folk; taught internationally from the 1960s
card.profile: A line/chain horo from Pazardzhik county in Western Thrace, central Bulgaria, in a complex 15/16 meter counted 2+2+2+2+3+2+2. Danced in an open circle with a front belt-hold (lesa na poyas), men typically at both ends with women in the middle. Styling is flat-footed, low and small-stepped with a constant knee-flex bounce; the figure moves side to side. Accompaniment ranges from a solo gaida (bagpipe) to a full folk band with tapan (Folk Dance Federation of California; Bulgarian folk dance, Wikipedia).
card.insight: Dick Crum speculated the name came from a now-lost song mentioning hemlock; today Bulgarians class it simply as a fast Thracian dance, introduced to North America by Dennis Boxell at the 1967 University of the Pacific Folk Dance Camp (Folk Dance Federation of California).
card.image_significance: Fifteen-sixteenths of pure Thrace. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — W. Thrace (Pazardzhik), Bulgaria.
